title: Paired series — coverage-usage and contested
description: The fourth data layer. Which series pair with which, which side is which, and what each side should be called are research judgements, not display choices — the same class of knowledge as caveat and unmeasured, both of which were moved out of code for this reason. Built when the trigger set in log cycle 31j fired: a second domain (employment) required absence-pairs.

kind.description: coverage-usage is ASYMMETRIC — a records what was delivered, b what it converted into, and the order is the argument. contested is SYMMETRIC — two instruments measuring the same thing that disagree, where neither answers the other and neither may be shown alone.

domain.description:
The subject area a record belongs to. A TAG SET, not a partition: a ledger record carries `domains[]` and may carry several, a series carries exactly one, and a phase is not a domain — phase 7 produced eight records filed across seven values.

THE DISTINCTION THAT GETS CONFUSED IS welfare AGAINST human-development: welfare is the DELIVERY of a scheme, human-development is the OUTCOME it was meant to produce. Records carrying both (Swachh Bharat, PM-JAY, the anaemia reversal) are the normal case, not an error — the scheme is one domain and what it did to people is another.
- macro: aggregate economic conditions and fiscal or monetary policy.
- banking: banks, credit, financial supervision and resolution.
- employment: work, labour force, earnings and formality.
- poverty: measured deprivation and consumption-based poverty.
- human-development: outcomes in health, nutrition and survival — what delivery produced.
- infrastructure: physical networks and their capacity or service.
- welfare: scheme delivery and entitlements — what was provided.
- governance: institutions of state, enforcement, transparency and rights.
- kashmir: a cross-cutting lens, applied to records whose primary subject sits elsewhere.
- federalism: Centre-state relations. Also a lens: GST and groundwater carry it alongside their own subject.
- foreign: trade, external balances and relations with other states.
- defence: military and security. One record; sparsely attested.
- environment: land, water, air and the resource base.
- demography: population structure. NEVER USED — no record or series carries it, so its intended boundary is unattested and this line describes the word, not observed practice.

framing.description: One sentence, specific to this pair. A standing sentence about connections and taps would misdescribe a road network.

gapReason.description: Required when gapComputable is false. Why subtraction is not available — different quantities, different denominators, different populations, or a disagreement rather than a gap.

title.description: Short name for the pair, as authored. The framing is the sentence; this is the handle.

ledgerRefs.description: Ledger records this pair bears on.

status.description: live (default) means both sides resolve and the pair renders. declared-pending means the pair is recorded as OWED — the research judgement that these two things belong side by side has been made, but at least one side is not yet authored. A pending pair renders nowhere; it is held so the gap is visible as owed rather than silently absent.

side.description: Exactly one of series, absenceFrom or competingAccountsFrom must be set, unless the pair is declared-pending, in which case a side may carry a label alone.

absenceFrom.description: Series or ledger id whose unmeasured declaration occupies this position — the counterpart does not exist and that is the finding.

competingAccountsFrom.description: Provenance id whose competingAccounts occupy this position — the counterpart is a dispute between sources, not a series.

label.description: What this side IS. Hand-written per pair and never generic: 'The build record' is not 'sustained use'.
